Text:
A user makes the following post on a social media site:

How to get yourself to let go and throw donate worthy items away?
In the process of preparing my house to host of Thanksgiving I was forced to face how much excess stuff we have. I own my grandparents old place which came with all of the things. I did a big clean out prior but then I got to the hard stuff and needed to take a break and never went back to it. I decided we have enough true trash items we can just get a dumpster. However, we do have a fair amount of stuff I'm not touching. I don't like selling on fbook because I don't like people coming to my house and am not going to take the time to meet up somewhere. I'm in the country so donation places aren't crazy far but it's still like a 40 minute round trip. Also there are not donation pick ups in my location either. I have accepted I just need to throw it away so I can just breath and bring the ease I need. But I can have a hard time throwing away usable items. But I don't have the energy to deal with donating all of the stuff and taking hours to do so. Every place that does donation pickups do not come to my address.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I totally hear you. I’ve been in a similar situation with my parents’ stuff after they passed. At first, everything felt like it had to be saved or sent to the right place, but eventually, I realized the mental toll it was taking. Sometimes you have to make peace with the decision to let things go in a way that works for you. If it frees up your space and your mind, it’s worth it. To ease into it, I started boxing stuff up and labeling it with the intention of donating, but if it stayed in the trunk of my car for more than a month, I decided it was time to throw it out. Also, some friends in the city loved it when I brought over a box of random goodies. Turning it into a community swapping kind of thing made it feel less wasteful. If you want to get a bit of help, maybe you could consider asking someone you trust or hiring a local college student. They’re often looking for small gigs and could help with pickups or sorting. It won’t solve everything, but it’s nice to have company while dealing with all that stuff. Doing it alone can be pretty overwhelming, honestly. It’s just one of those things where you’ll probably feel a lot better once you’ve cleared it out a bit. Just chip away at it little by little and try not to stress. It’s alright to prioritize what brings you peace first, y’know?

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Guys! I need help! Need a vanity bulb E26 5W, DC12V compatible in daylight and Frosted.
Long story short. I broke one of the vanity globe light bulbs, so I figured i go into Home Deport and get a replacement. Came home to realize that it wasn't the same voltage. So I need something that is compatible with DC12V. Thanks!



They receive the following reply to their post:

I’ve totally been there. Like, you grab a bulb thinking, “ah, lighting is lighting,” only to realize there’s this whole universe of technical specifications. Honestly, it sounds like you’re dealing with more specialized stuff than I usually have lying around. I once went through a similar saga with my aquarium lights. I thought “bulb is a bulb,” but man, was I wrong! I ended up at this tiny specialty shop run by this guy who took lighting way too seriously. He got me set up, though. I’d say try searching online, maybe Amazon or a specialty lighting store. They usually list all the nitty-gritty details so you can match it up perfectly. You might even want to reach out to the manufacturer of the original fixture, see if they recommend something. By the time I finally got the right one for my aquarium, the fish seemed to be judging me… so best of luck!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

I just rewatched Grease 1978 for the first time since… middle school. I loved the music and fashion, wasn’t a fan of the way Danny treated Sandy.
I felt so badly for her all throughout. I really thought she could have done better. Their entanglement wouldn’t have lasted. She was so much kinder to him than he was to her. That poor thing. I simply adored the songs however, and it was funny at points. It’s enjoyable, I just feel like he should have done a LOT more to win her over.



They receive the following reply to their post:

Honestly, you're spot on about how Danny treated Sandy. But let's be real—Grease was from a different time, and people back then had some odd ideas about relationships. It’s bizarre how changing yourself for someone else was just shrugged off like it's no big deal. Sandy didn’t need to turn into someone else for a guy like Danny. The music slaps though, no doubt about it. But I still wonder why everyone glorifies that "bad boy changes for love" trope. In real life, that nonsense never works!

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

What’s something that always makes you laugh, no matter how bad your day is?
We all need something that can bring us out of a funk, even on tough days. Whether it’s a favorite joke, TV show, or memory, what’s your go-to source of laughter when you’re feeling down?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Honestly, I have this video of a cat trying to jump onto a counter and totally missing. The way it gracefully slides off just cracks me up every single time. It's like the cat thought it was athletic, but nope, gravity had other plans. Also, reruns of The Office can really get me laughing, especially when Michael does something totally cringe-worthy or Dwight is just being Dwight. Oh, and my friend, Jake, has this bizarre talent for making the most ridiculous faces. He can be super expressive, like Jim Carrey-level, and when he starts, it’s impossible not to laugh. It's good to have a few go-tos, you know? You never know what will save your mood on a rainy day.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Joint Venture/Partnership - My 5 years Digital Marketing (PPC) Experience + Your Sales Skills or your Clients
I am an Digital Marketing Manager with over 5 years of Agency experience (Over $10Mn+ in ad spend). For the past five years, Facebook Ads and Google ads have been my bread and butter. I am willing to provide proof of my past/current work. Currently, I’m working full-time at a small agency (think old-school clients who don’t even know what CPC/CPM is). However, I’ve got spare time on the side that I’m eager to dedicate to a Joint Venture/Partnership. My stronger side - Tech & My weaker side - Sales What I’m looking for: * Someone who’s skilled in sales/outreach or has access to potential clients but needs a partner to handle the service delivery side of things. * A collaborative partnership where I focus on managing and scaling campaigns, while you handle client acquisition. If this sounds like something you’d be interested in, comment below or slide in my DMs.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I get it, teaming up with someone in sales sounds like a good idea. I mean, sometimes folks who are all about numbers and data—like you with PPC—don’t always want to spend time doing the people-y stuff. It’s like asking a polar bear to survive in the desert. I’ve got a buddy who’s really good at sales and he’s never met a person he couldn’t chat up. Meanwhile, I’m over here, always worried about whether I'm using the right stovetop burner for my pasta. So if you can find the right partner, that's Ramen turning into filet mignon faster than you can say ‘monthly analytics report.’ Sometimes the trick is just asking around, or hitting up networking events where these ‘sales whale’ people hang out. It's not magic, but it also kinda is.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Acrylic is the overall best fibre for yarn
I'm gonna speak my truth. Big wool can't silence me. Now obviously yes different fibres have things they are best at I know I know I am finishing up a cotton blanket. I know this. BUT. Acrylic is the most versatile. It's the easiest to care for. A huge spectrum in terms of feel. Any colour any shade. There's very few things you *cant* make with acrylic. It's not all the cheap nasty stuff anymore! We live in the future! The softest yarns I've ever felt? ACRYLIC. if you really REALLY need a quality of natural fibres? ACRYLIC BLENDS. and it's cheaper. Come on. Also this bit is very much personal taste but I think acrylic has the best level of slippyness for me. Doesn't slip off the hook or needle too easily, just enough drag to keep it under control without making the friction a problem. Obviously there's some variation by brand etc. And like I say other yarns are good I've been really enjoying cotton lately, sidar happy cotton is lovely (if a bit splitty). I've had some lovely bamboos and even a bit of cashmere. But acrylic is king. Bring on the pitchforks.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I gotta agree with you there! I’m not a master knitter or anything, but acrylic has been my go-to whenever I’ve tried to make those DIY crafts look halfway decent. I feel like whenever I’m at a craft store, I gravitate to the acrylic section because there’s just so much choice. And man, it’s like you’re saying – the color range is wild. You want neon green? They got it. A shade of blue that looks like the ocean but not quite tropical ocean – more like an ocean on a cloudy day? Yeah, they got that too. I had this old sweater I’d made out of acrylic. It was so comfy! I couldn't tell if it was acrylic or unicorn fluff. And the best part? I could throw it in the washing machine without a second thought. It’s a lifesaver for someone like me who doesn’t have the patience to hand wash. Also, I’ll be honest, I’m not rolling in money, so getting the most bang for my buck is always a big deal. Sure, those natural fibers feel fancy and all, but acrylic gets the job done without making me feel like I’m knitting with gold bars. It’s like the humble hero of the yarn world, just doing its job and doing it well. I wonder if one day there’ll be yarn that can double as a WiFi antenna. That’d be neat.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

I need some brutal spells
I’m making a dark fantasy story with 4 types of magic, including magic books/Grimoires, Mystic Crystal’s that power technology and weapons, Rune magic which requires you to carve symbols in your arm, and Glyph magic where you use a magical brush that makes Glyphs out of energy. The magic has the basic 4 elements water, fire, earth, and air and any other type of magic you can think of and I want some really realistic and brutal spells but I can’t think of any.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I think you’re overthinking it. When I first started, I got hung up on making my magic systems super unique too, but the story got way better when I started caring more about my characters. You gotta remember it’s about how magic affects them. Once you figure that out, it’s easier to fit in all the cool spells. And for brutality, well, as long as any injury or death from a spell fits into the larger story arc, you’re golden. One time in a campaign I ran, there was a character who used Rune magic, but every time they cast a spell, it took a physical toll, like bleeding out or the runes literally burning up their skin. They had to choose when it was worth the pain. You get character moments and brutal scenes for free with that kinda stuff. And for the crystal-powered tech, maybe it’s so unstable it leaves a trail of destruction wherever it’s used. You get tension and action just from that unpredictability. Anyway, you don't have to go all out on dark or brutal. It’s about what serves their journeys. Where are my car keys...hmmm.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Everything I have bought lately has been garbage
I’m going to a family’s member’s wedding in a few weeks and bought a dress on a secondhand app. It is the most ill-fitting thing I’ve ever purchased. I’m going to wear a dress I had in my closet but forgot about. I made them a gift and bought a frame for it. I have been looking at thrift stores for a few months but haven’t found a frame the right size. I bought a multi-pack of frames at a big box store because they were exactly the size and color I needed and I figure I’d use the rest of the frames myself. Somehow I didn’t realize the pane is plastic, not glass. (That’s on me) The gift I spent a month on looks like trash in it. I tried to save money by buying a frame but now I’m going to have to take it to the frame shop to get a custom frame anyway. Idk this whole experience has been a reminder that you don’t need whatever that thing is. You probably already have what you need or you just need to do whatever the equivalent of getting a custom frame is. Buying stuff isn’t the answer.



They receive the following reply to their post:

Yeah, it can be super frustrating when things don’t work out as planned, especially with shopping. I’ve had similar experiences where I thought something was a steal but it just turned out to be more trouble than it was worth. You know, I’ve got all these mugs because I thought each one was perfect in the moment, but now they’re just filling up space in my cabinet. It’s like, do I need another mug to make my coffee taste better? Probably not. I really started noticing that I didn’t need as much as I thought I did. Especially when I travel, I realize I can get by with much less, and yet, I come home and think about all the stuff sitting in my closet. Sometimes it’s just about finding a creative solution with what you have, and letting go of the impulse to buy more can be freeing, but yeah, I get it’s not easy when you really want something to look or feel right. You just gotta roll with it sometimes.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Sometimes ill be at the gym or out for a run and I’ll think something like: “if I don’t reach 15 reps the girl I’m seeing will break up with me” “If I stop running, I’ll fail my exam next week” I’m not even overly superstitious but when I do this I’m really convinced the bad thing might happen if I don’t reach my goal, sometimes I’ll think it and then be annoyed at myself because as soon as I do, it’s like I’ve put serious pressure on myself. They receive the following reply to their post:

Spooky gym magic.

Well we know that the town of whovillre, and the people that are in it I absolutely microscopic, if I recall correctly, the whole town is either inside a snowflake, or a speck of dust on a clover Roast beast, seems like the equivalent of roast beef, and beef is meat What is meat? It is muscle tissue from an animal/insects etc And no, don't try to pull the excuse that they are eating single-celled organs or bacteria j single celled organisms do not have meat, but are< rather filled with this disgusting jelly like fluid and maybe a nucleas The only creature that small that has actual muscles inside it would be tardigrades, which this can be accurately assumed because they are most closely related to arthropods So yeah, the who's are eating tardigrades on Christmas dinner I wonder what that tastes like



They receive the following reply to their post:

OMG, I love this! Tardigrades, that's something I never would have connected with roast beast, but it totally makes sense when you think about it! Honestly, if Whoville is as tiny as a speck of dust, what else could they be feasting on, right? I mean, how different could a tardigrade feast be from us having a turkey? It’s like their perfect little bite-sized turkey. I do wonder what tardigrades would taste like, though. Surely Dr. Seuss didn't realize the depth of the dining experience he was hinting at with all these microscopic feasts! Now I'm just picturing Whoville as a sort of gourmet hot spot for tiny creatures. Makes me think of how we really shouldn’t underestimate the small things. Gosh, who knew talking about tardigrades could make me hungry??

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is worth a watch if you like Spider-Man comics
It seems like anytime I post about something that I like it gets downvoted because people think I'm a shill. Take a look at the subs that I post in if you think I am. I'm not. "But that's exactly what a shill would say" okay sure. I just finished watching episode 1 and 2 of this show. I was skeptical. A lot of Spider-Man cartoons over the past decade have been very kid-focused with a lot of lame DreamWorks-style jokes. This one feels like it's written by actual people who care about Spider-Man, not Disney writers who are trying to appeal to 11-year-olds. They take some of the standard Spider-Man tropes and toss them out. The animation style is more reminiscent of Kirby than recent cartoons. Most surprising casting choice: Paul F. Tompkins as one of the Oscorp scientists.



They receive the following reply to their post:

Hey, I’m with you on this! As a long-time Spider-Man fan who’s seen a ton of adaptations, it's refreshing when a new show feels true to the comics. I totally get the skepticism. I mean, I’ve been burned by more than a few Spider-Man cartoons that seemed more interested in selling action figures than telling a good story. But I’m with you, this one feels different. It’s like they actually read the comics and understood why we love Spider-Man in the first place. And the animation—you’re so right, it’s got that Kirby vibe, with a style that’s its own thing rather than copying what’s popular. As for Paul F. Tompkins, I didn’t expect to hear his voice in a Spider-Man show, but I’m pretty curious now. He’s hilarious in pretty much everything he’s in, so I guess seeing him in the Oscorp role will be interesting. And trust me, the only shill here is me trying to talk my friends into watching good shows.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

IWTL how to become a more dedicated person towards studying
Currently, I have goals to achieve, rewards and reasons to do it, but I just can't do it, it isn't attractive enough for me to *WANT* to do it, and when I do do it, it isn't very helpful and I barely learn



They receive the following reply to their post:

Oh man, I get what you’re saying. Back in college, I had the hardest time focusing on studying stuff that didn’t really interest me, even if it was important for my degree. Here's what helped me a bit: first, try breaking down your goals into really small, manageable tasks. Like, instead of saying “I have to study for that giant test,” just say “Today, I’ll read just this one chapter,” or “I’ll solve five sample problems before I take a break.” That way, it doesn’t feel like such a massive mountain to climb. Also, I found that changing my study environment made a big difference. Sometimes just moving to a different room or studying outside can change my mood and help me focus better. As for wanting to do it, maybe try to make it a habit to reward yourself, even with small things, after you've ticked off a task. Like munching on your favorite snack or watching an episode of a show you like. Also, studying with friends or in groups can mix in some fun – we used to have study meets where after 30 mins of studying, we’d play board games for a break. Find what small changes work for you and tweak your routine until you hit that sweet spot.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

DAE like feeling stressed
When I have a lot of things to do, no matter how much/little time I have to finish them, I get this strange mix of nerves and excitement. It’s like a tight feeling in my stomach and a pressure in my throat, but somehow it feels good, almost like a rush. No matter how dire the task(s). It’s similar to the feeling of being on a rollercoaster or like butterflies in your stomach. I feel light, giggly, and full of energy. It doesn’t matter whether I’m procrastinating or actually getting things done, the feeling is always there, though it eventually fades after a while. Is this some kind of adrenaline rush? Am I alone in this? And do any of you have a clue to why this response occurs? (After typing this out I quickly wanna add that I don't do drugs lol)



They receive the following reply to their post:

Oh man, I totally get that. I have this weird love-hate relationship with stress too. It's like being on the edge of a cliff but still feeling kind of exhilarated, you know? I've heard some folks call it the 'thrill of the deadline'. I guess it might just be how some of us are wired. Like I remember back in college cramming for exams—my nerves would be all over the place, but there was this rush of energy that just made me feel like I was invincible. Then I'd crash once the task was done. I think it's partly about that adrenaline you mentioned. It's our body's way of pushing us to face challenges. It helps us stay focused and alert. But over time, I've learned to balance that feeling, 'cause while it's awesome to feel energized and on top of the world, it can also be exhausting. I try to manage those feelings by giving myself little breaks to decompress, but I do enjoy those stress-fueled moments of crazy productivity. I wonder if it's some kind of survival mechanism? Like, our ancestors had to deal with danger and the fight-or-flight response was key, but now we get that same kick out of less life-threatening situations, like work or school tasks. Interesting how our bodies adapt, right?

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Dash & Lily
My teen daughter is really loving Dash & Lily. There is only one season (2020). Is there anything out there that’s similar?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Ah, Dash & Lily is such a sweet series. I watched it with my niece, and we loved how lighthearted and fun it was. If your daughter liked that, she might enjoy “The Holiday Calendar.” It’s a cute Netflix movie with a charming vibe. And then there’s “To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before,” which kind of became a big deal when it came out. It’s got that same kind of sweet romance without being too over the top. Another series is “Never Have I Ever,” created by Mindy Kaling. It’s got a nice mix of humor and heart, plus some fun coming-of-age vibes your daughter might enjoy. I remember watching it and finding it surprisingly touching, plus it made me laugh out loud a few times. And then there's “Atypical,” which, while a bit different, balances comedy and serious themes quite nicely. It’s more about family dynamics, but the humor and warmth could be right up the same alley. Give any of those a try, could be a hit! I'm still thinking of what else might work, but those are definitely some good starting points.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

I don’t think I’ve ever seen two cars at a red light with their blinkers synchronized
Ever since I was a kid I would always watch the cars in turn lanes and see if any of the blinkers matched up. I don’t think I ever have. They eventually get out of sync. Maybe someday…



They receive the following reply to their post:

You know, I’ve noticed that too! It’s like a little puzzle to watch them flash almost in time and then drift apart. When I was a teenager, I’d sometimes sit in parking lots just spacing out, and I'd watch those lights. I’d try to capture the exact moment they’d line up but they never really stay in sync—you’re spot on. I think it’s something about the natural timing—every car’s cycle is slightly different, and maybe they start to sync up, but then they slip out of time again. Almost like how people can fall into a rhythm, then do their own thing. I wonder if there are other things like that out there. What other small things line up perfectly only to drift apart again almost immediately?

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

bag suggestions?
Hi everybody, I’m set on my first backpacking trip to Europe in a couple months and I’ve been having a hard time deciding on a bag. I’m gonna be away for a couple months so I’m thinking 40-45 liters is enough, although I do want to wear a smaller bag (maybe like 15l) in front so it can double as a carry-on and a portable daypack. The two sets I’ve been looking into are: -Gregory Zulu 45 + Nano 18 -Osprey Farpoint 40 + Farpoint Daypack The Farpoint seems like the easy choice, what with its travel-friendly features like carry-on size, lockable zippers, and compatibility with the daypack (the daypack is attachable to the main bag). When I tried on the Zulu though, I felt more comfortable, mostly because it wasn’t as thick as the farpoint. Should I go for the features of the farpoint, or the looks and comfortability of the Zulu? Or if you have any other suggestions, all are welcome.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I think comfort really matters for a trip that long, especially if you're walking or standing a lot. I've been on a few long trips, and honestly, a bag that's snug and comfy makes such a difference, even if it means you carry an extra lock just to make sure it’s secure. I had a 42L once that was super comfy like the Zulu. It felt lighter on my shoulders than some other bulkier packs I'd tried. Bring a durable cable lock and some packing cubes if you’re worried about organization. Just helps keep everything tidy. Compatibility with a smaller pack is a neat feature but not a deal breaker. With the Zulu, you could probably find a small daypack that clips onto, or fits nicely under, the main pack. Flexibility is key, you know? Only potential downside of less packable hiking bags is sometimes the front-loading isn't as accessible, but you can pack strategically. Also, when I used a smaller pack for city exploring, carrying it on the front of my body got annoying unless it was a quick trip...so something slim is better. Given you're gonna lug this around for a couple of months, I'd just go with whatever feels best because you'll notice discomfort every time you wear it. You’ll figure out pretty quick if you need to adjust how you pack it— I had to get good at organizing my pack by what I needed regular quick access to vs the random stuff I didn’t think about much like backup toiletries or gear. Anyway, maybe mix and keep trying your options, you might find a combo you prefer by size.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

Mickey17- ain’t no reason for Kai to be at the Dinner
(Caveat: I’ve not read the book, have just watched the movie and evaluating based on that) For the longest time, I didn’t understand why Kai was at the steak dinner which was meant to test the new food replacements. I thought they were trying to pair Kai with Mickey but it seems like they just brought her along to tell her genes were good- is that it? Seems pointless…? Mickey could have bumped into her enroute back to his bunk, then opening to the next scene. Am I missing something?



They receive the following reply to their post:

Ah, yeah, I hear you on that one. It's those little things in movies that can leave you scratching your head. Based on how you described it, it does seem a bit odd for Kai to be there if her role in the dinner is just about genes or whatever. Maybe they were trying to build a sense of connection or intrigue between Kai and Mickey, but it wasn’t as clear or effective as it could’ve been in the movie. I remember watching a few movies where scenes just kinda happen, and you’re sitting there thinking, “Did I miss something?” But sometimes it's also about how directors or writers try to cram in exposition or character development. If the scene felt pointless, maybe it just didn’t translate well from the book or got lost in editing. Seeing someone just pop into a scene with no apparent reason can throw you off. Maybe reading the book could shed some light, but yeah, I feel your confusion on this one.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

A Man I Could Love
I made a deal with the devil when the gods failed to countervail my cries. He answered on my first knock, with a friendly smile that twinkled his eyes. For the Devil is beautiful, skin as white as paper with eyes as clear as ice, a man I could love. The devil too is a god, a god who offers me the world, for a price. For life isn't fed on sliver spoons forever, you need to learn to eat it bare handedly.



They receive the following reply to their post:

I can see what you’re reaching for here, blending this idea of temptation with beauty, but it almost feels like it’s only been through one draft. I mean, I think it needs a bit more, you know? More depth in the imagery to really bring it to life. When you say, “skin as white as paper with eyes as clear as ice,” it’s cool and all, but it feels like something I’ve seen before. It might be more intriguing if you flipped something like that on its head and showed us what’s unexpected about this devil instead of the typical stuff. Also, the bit about ‘a man I could love’ could dig deeper. Maybe explore what that love looks like, or maybe how it conflicts with the idea of making a pact with the devil. 'Cause love and deals with the devil have been done a lot, so maybe just spend more time exploring a new angle in there. It could be something as small as a simple quirky habit or something really human. That's often where the unimaginable empathy can be found. And the whole “for life isn’t fed on silver spoons” thing, maybe lean into that too? Like, give us a snapshot of what eating barehandedly really feels like, ‘cause right now it feels kinda broad. A personal anecdote or a vivid moment can make a big difference in how a reader connects. I dunno, I just feel like you’re on the cusp of something maybe really interesting.

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

just got my first contract!
got reached out to over NPX! i’ve been on there a year and nothing has ever come of it, but this week my one-act play was offered a 4 show run at a professional theater! The rights were purchased (i didn’t ask for much because the shows are donation only). This is just to say update your NPX with details and marketable tags and KEEP AT IT! So excited for the production (i get to be involved too!!)



They receive the following reply to their post:

Hey, that is soooo frickin' awesome! Even if it took a while, it's proof that something worth waiting for can really happen. NPX sounds like a really tough crowd to break into, so the fact that you've managed to get noticed is huge. Getting to be involved with the production, too? That sounds like a blast. I reckon that’ll be way more fulfilling than just signing off on some paperwork and never being around to see it live. I’m curious, do you feel like there was a specific change or tag that got people to notice your work, or do you feel like you just finally got lucky with the right person seeing it at the right time?

A user makes the following post on a social media site:

"My Name is Toast"
Everything went dark as arms wrapped right around me. I didnt feel alarmed, I knew they would not hurt me. I dont know how I knew this, but their voice had clearly read.. Their intention was to love me, to love me until im dead. It took some time to learn that this was now my home. For as long as I'm alive, I know I'll never be alone. I know this human loves me, they tell me every day and night. If only I could talk like them... But for now, I meow, and purr so loud, and hope one day I might. (This is only my second poem go easy on me 🥲)



They receive the following reply to their post:

Hey, that's a super sweet poem you’ve got there! It's got that comforting and warm vibe, like having a cozy little kitty nap with a soft blanket. I remember when I first got my cat, the bond just felt so natural. There’s nothing like a cat jumping on your lap and purring to instantly make the world seem a bit better, you know?
